01 / THE BIG PICTURE

One contract. Two deliverables.

Start with the mental model. Then open any layer and read the code behind it.

RUNTIME / WRAITH

Your logic, inside a component.

Axum receives JSON. Wasmtime creates a fresh Store and calls the guest's run export. HTTP, TCP, and events cross the boundary only through explicit host imports.

RustWASI P2SQLiteRhai
Trace the architecture →
APPLIANCE / WRAITHOS

The same binary, closer to the metal.

Buildroot definitions package the runtime into a read-only root filesystem. Persistent data lives separately. ARM adds a trial-boot contract, health proof, and watchdog recovery.

BuildrootSquashFSA/B slotsARM64

03 / CONCURRENCY LAB

Two permits. Six requests. Who waits?

DETERMINISTIC MODEL

All requests arrive together in this simplified FIFO model. Adjust the global pool to see waiting, execution, and timeout. Real Tokio scheduling, tenant gates, and HTTP overhead are not modeled.

t = 0.0 s6 waiting · 0 running · 0 completed

With two permits and a three-second wait budget, the last two requests time out in this scenario.

04 / ARM BOOT LAB

An update gets three chances.

GRUB STATE MACHINE

Stage slot B, reboot through its trial attempts, or commit after a healthy boot. This lab models GRUB's counter—not watchdog wall-clock timing, disk writes, or power-loss behavior.

INITIAL STATE
ESP / 200 MiBGRUB + Image-a / Image-bPersistent boot state
SLOT A/dev/vda264 MiB · SquashFSACTIVE · GOOD
SLOT B/dev/vda364 MiB · SquashFSINACTIVE
DATA / 128 MiBDB · modules · configurationShared across root slots
GRUB ENVIRONMENT
Slot A is committed. Stage a trial to begin.

Leave a trial uncommitted and reboot until tries reaches zero. The next reboot selects the last-known-good slot. The real watchdog can demote after its grace period; that timing is outside this model.

2.96%

The execution timer is only one part of the request.

About 2.96% of the 6.10 ms client mean falls inside the reported execution interval. The remainder is not individually attributed. HTTP, quota work, TCP setup, curl process overhead, and scheduling all live outside that timer.

Inspect provenance, raw values, and limitations

Not independently rerun. The checkout's crate version is 0.1.0; the exact benchmark commit and binary hash were not supplied. The benchmark guest is not the checked-in sample.

ENGINEERING, WITHOUT THE HAND-WAVING

A strong project shows its boundaries.

Wraith already contains real sandboxing, resource gates, observability, and appliance recovery mechanisms. It is not yet an audited hostile multi-tenant platform. Authentication, signature persistence, event visibility, and setup integration have documented gaps.
